title: Multimodal UAV Cybersecurity Copilot
summary: A research and simulation environment that fuses MAVLink telemetry, network sensor events, STIX 2.1 threat intelligence, mission logs, manuals, and imagery into evidence-backed investigations mapped to ATT&CK.
primaryMessage: I combine doctoral UAV cybersecurity research with applied AI, threat intelligence, streaming data, and multimodal reasoning.
notice: Research and simulation environment. Not a flight-safety-certified product, not for operational flight decisions, and all attacks are simulated.

executive.problem: When a drone behaves oddly, an analyst must correlate flight telemetry, network alerts, threat intelligence, mission logs, and imagery by hand. That takes time, and the evidence is easy to miss.
executive.approach: A copilot that streams telemetry and network events, detects suspicious patterns, links them to threat intelligence and ATT&CK techniques in a knowledge graph, and drafts an investigation where every claim points to its evidence.
executive.impact: Analysts start from a correlated, cited timeline instead of five separate tools. The environment injects simulated attacks so detection and investigation quality can be measured.
executive.whyItMatters: This is the differentiating project: doctoral-level UAV security research joined with streaming data, knowledge graphs, and multimodal AI, presented with the limits of a research environment.

problem: UAV attacks such as GPS spoofing, command injection over MAVLink, telemetry jamming, and ground-station compromise leave traces in different places: flight telemetry, network traffic, and mission records. Threat intelligence about them is scattered and rarely expressed in a form tools can reason over. Analysts need correlation and explanation, and researchers need a repeatable environment to test detection methods.
users: Security analysts investigating UAV incidents in a lab or range
Threat-intelligence analysts modelling UAV-specific adversary behavior

constraints.detail: Simulation only. Outputs are investigative aids, never flight-control commands.
Every statement in an investigation must cite a telemetry window, sensor event, intelligence object, document passage, or frame.
Streaming detection keeps up with telemetry rates in the simulator.
Uses public or synthetic data; no operational mission data.

zones.label: Simulation environment: SITL flight stack and simulated attacks

architectureNotes: Telemetry and network events share one stream so detectors can correlate across sources on a common clock.
Detections become graph nodes linked to STIX indicators, UAV-specific attack patterns, and ATT&CK techniques.
The investigation agent retrieves from the graph and indexes, then writes findings that each carry evidence IDs the analyst can open.
The attack injector records ground truth so every simulated incident can be scored.

aiTechnique.choice: Streaming detection plus GraphRAG and a multimodal model inside a bounded investigation agent.
aiTechnique.rationale: Attacks are relational: a spoofed position, a network alert, and an intelligence report matter together. A knowledge graph captures those relations and GraphRAG retrieves connected evidence. Imagery and manuals need a multimodal model. Detection itself stays in rules and anomaly models so it is fast and testable.

rejected.reason: Loses the relationships between indicators, techniques, and observed events.
Too slow and inconsistent for streaming telemetry.

implementation.detail: ArduPilot or PX4 SITL with a ground station; scripted attack scenarios such as GPS spoofing and MAVLink command injection.
Suricata and Zeek on the simulated network, with custom rules for MAVLink traffic.
Kafka-compatible stream with detectors for telemetry physics checks, command anomalies, and sensor alerts.
STIX 2.1 objects with custom extensions for UAV assets and observables, mapped to ATT&CK techniques.
Neo4j graph of assets, observables, indicators, techniques, and detections.
Bounded agent with graph, index, and evidence tools; output schema requires evidence IDs per finding.
docker-compose stack for simulator, sensors, stream, graph, and services.

datasets: Scripted attack scenarios with injector ground truth
Benign flight scenarios for false-positive measurement
baselines: Vector RAG investigation without the graph

metrics.name: Detection rate by attack type
metrics.method: Match detections to injector ground truth within a time window

metrics.name: False positives per flight hour
metrics.method: Count alerts on flights with no injected attack

metrics.name: Technique mapping accuracy
metrics.target: Share of incidents mapped to the correct ATT&CK technique
metrics.method: Compare mapped technique to scenario label

metrics.name: Evidence-supported findings
metrics.target: Share of report findings whose cited evidence supports them
metrics.method: Reviewer check of each finding against cited evidence

metrics.name: Investigation time
metrics.target: Analyst time to a correct root cause, with and without the copilot

regression: Scenario suite reruns on detector, graph schema, or model change
Report schema test: findings without evidence IDs fail
failureAnalysis: Missed attacks reviewed by telemetry signature
Wrong technique mappings reviewed against graph coverage

humanControl.detail: The copilot drafts findings; the analyst confirms, edits, or rejects each one.
Every finding opens to the raw telemetry window, event, intel object, passage, or frame.
The system has no interface to send commands to a vehicle.

expected: Higher technique-mapping accuracy with the graph than with vector retrieval alone
Reduced investigation time, unverified until a timed study is run

limitations: Simulation only; not validated on real vehicles, real RF environments, or operational networks.
Not a flight-safety-certified product and must not inform flight decisions.
Scripted attacks cover a limited set of techniques.
Investigation-time benefit is unverified until measured.

setup: docker compose exec copilot python -m investigate --latest
reproduction.testData: Scenario scripts, public ATT&CK data, sample STIX bundles, and public manufacturer documentation references.
reproduction.expectedOutput: Detections on the stream, a graph subgraph for the incident, and a cited investigation report.
